trace.title: HTTP and filters
trace.detail: An HTTP endpoint is a boundary. Treat incoming strings and JSON as untrusted input. Binding turns JSON into Java values. Validation checks those values. Authorization checks whether this caller may perform this action. These are separate steps.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
A servlet filter can run before MVC. DispatcherServlet chooses a handler. A message converter reads JSON. Validation runs on the bound input. Then the controller invokes the service. The response converter writes JSON.

Try an empty title, malformed JSON, a valid request, and a simulated service conflict. For each, predict whether the service should run. Use @RestControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler for your domain errors. Log a request ID so an operator can find details privately.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: Returning an entity can trigger lazy queries during JSON serialization or reveal an internal field. A 200 response containing {error: ...} also makes clients guess whether the operation succeeded.
